title: How the US solar industry remains resilient through sharp swings in energy policy | Wood Mackenzie
gist: In a sponsored Energy Gang episode recorded at RE+ 2026, Ed Crooks talks with Shoals Technologies' Karen Bazela and Array Technologies' Jessica Lawrence-Vaca (whose companies have announced a merger) about how US solar stays resilient amid policy whiplash: data-centre power demand and 'speed to power' versus long gas-turbine lead times, plus the trade-offs of domestic manufacturing and the 45X credit's coverage of trackers but not EBOS.

insights.claim: US solar has stayed resilient despite dramatic shifts in Washington's energy priorities, helped by rapid growth in electricity demand from data centres; the key question for suppliers is now how fast they can bring new capacity online rather than how much they cut emissions.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: The solar investment case is shifting from climate policy to AI/data-centre power demand, making it less exposed to partisan swings.
insights.quote: The key question for solar suppliers now is not how far they can cut greenhouse gas emissions, but how fast they can bring new generation capacity on line.
insights.locator: Conditions have been challenging for the US solar industry

insights.claim: Long lead times for gas turbines and other generation technologies give solar a speed-to-power advantage in meeting near-term electricity demand while other sources come online.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Turbine backlogs are a tailwind for solar plus storage orders in the near term.
insights.locator: Karen and Jessica discuss speed to power

themes.theme: Consolidation in solar balance of system

insights.claim: Shoals Technologies and Array Technologies have announced a merger to create an integrated supplier for the solar and storage industries, combining electrical balance of system (EBOS) solutions and trackers.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Watch the Shoals-Array combination for cross-selling synergies and consolidation pressure on other BOS suppliers.
insights.locator: In this special episode from the RE+ conference

insights.claim: Shoals and Array executives argue the solar industry should push policymakers toward an all-of-the-above energy approach and permitting reform to expedite investment, and should advocate on American manufacturing, construction jobs, steel and energy security rather than only climate benefits.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Signals industry repositioning of messaging to survive Republican-led energy policy; permitting reform is a policy catalyst to watch.

insights.claim: Array Technologies makes 85 to 90 per cent of its components in the US and recently opened a $50 million facility in Albuquerque, while Shoals manufactures in the US but still sources some components overseas.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Domestic content levels affect tariff exposure and lead times; Array appears more insulated from import risk.
insights.quote: Array makes 85 to 90 per cent of its components in the US and recently opened a $50 million Albuquerque facility
insights.locator: The domestic supply chain offers shorter lead times

insights.claim: Solar trackers qualify for the US 45X manufacturing tax credit while electrical balance-of-systems equipment does not, and the guests argue policy should distinguish components worth producing in America from those that are not, since a fully domestic supply chain cannot be built overnight.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: 45X eligibility creates margin differences between tracker and EBOS makers — relevant to Array vs Shoals economics and the merged entity.
insights.quote: trackers qualify for the 45X manufacturing tax credit, while electrical balance-of-systems equipment does not
insights.locator: The domestic supply chain offers shorter lead times

insights.claim: Shoals and Array executives say the male-dominated solar industry needs to recruit more women and show them pathways into senior roles.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Workforce and talent pipeline is a soft factor; limited direct investment signal.
